name: Anti-globalization movement
summary: A loose network of movements opposing corporate-led globalization, as embodied in the WTO, IMF, World Bank and trade deals, which it says put profit above democracy, labor, the environment and local self-determination. Its mainstream wants democratic control of the economy, protection of commons and public services, debt cancellation and fair rules, and organizes through decentralized direct action and coalitions.
scope: The left or 'alter-globalization' mainstream of the Seattle (1999) to World Social Forum era, drawing on Klein, Chomsky, Shiva, Susan George and PGA-style hallmarks. It excludes the nationalist and Christian-right opponents of globalization, who share the label but not the internationalist, egalitarian outlook.

keyFigures.name: Vandana Shiva

keyFigures.name: Noam Chomsky

sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: PGA hallmarks rejecting the WTO and opposing capitalism, colonialism, racism and patriarchy; decentralized direct action.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Not a core demand, but the movement fights privatization of public services and treats health as a public good; inferred from that stance.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: The movement stresses decent labor standards and pay against races to the bottom, but a minimum-wage level is rarely its focus; inferred from labor concerns.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The movement rejects 'free market fundamentalism' and the commodification of everything, and wants democratic control over economic life.

public-ownership.rationale: Opposes privatizing utilities such as water (Bolivia case) and wants shared resources kept public, though it favors local and commons control over state ownership as such.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Tobin-tax and wealth-redistribution proposals associated with the movement imply higher taxation of capital and wealth, but general income taxes are not its main theme.

unions-good.rationale: Cross-border unionization and workers' rights are named as central to the movement, and unions are core members of its coalitions.

property-fundamental.rationale: Klein describes reclaiming the commons from private enclosure and opposes patenting of genes and seeds, so property is not treated as near-absolute; inferred.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Curbing the unaccountable power of multinationals, ending corporate personhood and imposing binding standards is the movement's defining demand.

cut-welfare.rationale: The movement opposes austerity and structural-adjustment cuts to public services, so welfare cuts are rejected.

worker-ownership.rationale: Examples such as worker-run reclaimed enterprises and the anarchist and socialist wings favor it, but reformist strands do not demand it; split but leaning yes.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Anti-authoritarian activists faced heavy policing and surveillance at summits; civil-liberties skepticism is inferred, not a stated plank.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Drug policy is not part of the movement's agenda and its wings (libertarian-left versus religious or nationalist) differ.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Not addressed; the left wing opposes racism but includes civil-libertarian anarchists wary of state speech laws.

strong-leader.rationale: The movement is explicitly horizontal, decentralized and suspicious of leaders and hierarchy, a 'coalition of coalitions'.

state-harmful.rationale: Anarchist currents say yes, but most participants want states and institutions to regain democratic regulatory power over corporations; majority disagrees.

limit-guns.rationale: Not a movement topic and no documented common position; inferred indifference.

empower-police-military.rationale: Activists faced police repression at Seattle and Genoa (where Carlo Giuliani was killed), and the movement is hostile to militarized policing.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not addressed by the movement and its feminist and labor wings are divided on it.

decide-locally.rationale: Localization, local self-determination and reclaiming local commons are recurring themes, in contrast to distant trade bodies.

rehabilitation.rationale: Not a stated plank; a social-justice orientation suggests support for rehabilitative justice.

traditional-family.rationale: The left-wing mainstream is socially progressive, though the nationalist and Christian-right strands that also oppose globalization would agree; the typical adherent leans no.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Not a core issue; the progressive social-justice mainstream would support it, while right-wing opponents of globalization would not.

abortion-legal.rationale: Inferred from the feminist and social-justice mainstream; the Christian-right strand dissents and the issue is peripheral.

more-religion-public.rationale: The mainstream is secular-left; the Christian right strand wants more, but the typical adherent does not.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: PGA-style hallmarks oppose racism and colonialism, and the global-justice mainstream takes anti-racism as a core value.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from feminist and anti-patriarchy commitments in the movement's hallmarks; not directly debated.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Opposition to cultural homogenization is common, but the left wing rejects nationalism while the nationalist wing champions national culture; genuinely split.

gradual-change.rationale: Activists favor direct action and say they 'aren't waiting for the revolution', pushing change from below rather than slow institutional reform.

reduce-immigration.rationale: The left mainstream, including the No Border network, rejects border restriction; nationalist parties that favor it are disowned by the movement.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: The movement attacks the WTO, IMF and World Bank as undemocratic; reformers want them democratized but not given more power as they stand.

free-trade.rationale: The movement's core slogan 'the world is not for sale' targets trade deals such as NAFTA, GATS and the FTAA as serving corporations.

nation-first.rationale: The left wing frames itself as internationalist solidarity; nationalist wings dissent but are rejected by the mainstream.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Not addressed directly; the movement opposed the Iraq war but human-rights-based intervention divides internationalists.

open-borders.rationale: The No Border network seeks an end to border controls and Graeber describes radicals favoring gradual dismantling of borders, though not all strands go that far.

limit-growth.rationale: Environmental and localist strands are growth-skeptical but 'degrowth' is not a stated platform; inferred from environmental concerns.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Environmental protection and climate action are a major concern across the alter-globalization movement.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Opposition to GM crops, patents and corporate biotechnology (Bove, Shiva) suggests skepticism of technology-as-fix; inferred.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Environmental and anti-corporate activists have generally opposed nuclear power, though it is not a stated movement plank.

revolution-justified.rationale: Anarchist and anti-capitalist wings say yes, while reformist wings and the 'not waiting for the revolution' ethos point to change by direct action; split.

experts-over-public.rationale: The movement's charge against global institutions is that unaccountable technocrats bypass democracy; it demands popular participation.

central-planning.rationale: Rejects both corporate markets and top-down control; favors local, participatory alternatives, so central planning is not endorsed.

socialized-markets.rationale: Alter-globalists 'do not necessarily oppose the free market' and want fair trade and public or worker ownership of key resources; inferred.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from redistributive aims; not a prominent demand.

basic-income.rationale: Not a documented movement demand; supporters exist but there is no consensus.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Nationalist wings favor protection, while the left favors fair-trade rules and standards rather than blanket tariffs; split.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Not a stated position; the movement wants democratic control of economic policy but is wary of state-led strategic investment.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Land reform and support for small farmers against agribusiness imply favoring small owners; Stiglitz and Korten are cited for land reform.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Only the anarchist or communist fringe holds this, and it is not a movement demand.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Not a position of the movement, which wants financial regulation such as a Tobin tax rather than abolition of central banks.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Not part of the movement's thought; it favors grassroots democracy over state-recognized bodies.

one-party-rule.rationale: The movement is plural, horizontal and committed to democracy; the WSF calls itself non-partisan.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from democratic and anti-hierarchy commitments.

democracy-best.rationale: Barlow and Klein frame the struggle as 'saving democracy' and the movement's central charge is that global institutions undermine democracy.

direct-votes.rationale: Participatory democracy is a stated value, but referendums on laws are not specifically demanded; inferred.

workers-councils.rationale: Anarchist and socialist wings favor councils; reformist and NGO wings want parliamentary accountability; split.

right-to-secede.rationale: No documented position; local self-determination themes cut both ways.

natural-rulers.rationale: Inconsistent with the movement's egalitarian, anti-elite and horizontal ethos.

political-violence-never.rationale: The movement is explicitly split between civil disobedience, tactical frivolity and confrontational wings, with riots at Seattle, Gothenburg and Genoa.

war-builds-character.rationale: The movement opposed the Iraq war and is internationalist and anti-militarist.

separate-church-state.rationale: The secular-left mainstream agrees, though the Christian-right strand differs; inferred.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Mainstream is secular; only a Christian-right strand, distinct from the global-justice mainstream, would agree.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Rejects privatization of public functions generally, which Klein describes as turning every activity into a commodity.

military-superiority.rationale: The movement is anti-militarist and criticizes great-power domination, so seeking superiority over rivals is rejected.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The left mainstream is universalist and disowns nationalist parties like the NPD and Golden Dawn that favor ethnic nations.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The socialist wing says yes, while reformists and environmentalists do not frame history that way; split.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Global-justice rhetoric about inequality points toward reducing disparities, though outcome equality is not formulated as a demand.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Indigenous struggles, such as against biopiracy and land grabs, feature prominently, and indigenous groups join movement coalitions.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Opposition to colonialism is explicit in some hallmarks, but reparations are not a stated demand; debt cancellation is the closer one.

civilizational-union.rationale: Not a movement idea; it prefers global solidarity across all peoples.

self-interest-moral.rationale: The movement attacks profit-first corporate behavior and the commodification of life in favor of solidarity and commons.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The movement emphasizes rights (workers, indigenous, people over trade), not duties first; inferred.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Environmental protection is a major concern, and Shiva-style critiques object to turning nature into property, but intrinsic value is not formally stated.

limit-population.rationale: Not addressed; justice-oriented activists tend to blame inequality and corporate practice rather than population.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Some green strands say so, but the mainstream targets corporate globalization rather than industrial civilization as such.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Hostile to corporate-driven disruption such as GM crops and patented life; inferred.

human-enhancement.rationale: No documented position; skepticism of corporate biotechnology suggests mild disagreement.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Inferred from the demand for democratic accountability against technocracy.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Independent media and activist networks favor privacy tools; inferred, not a documented plank.

restore-past-order.rationale: The left mainstream is forward-looking ('another world is possible'), not restorationist.

results-over-ideology.rationale: A values-driven movement, though pragmatic coalition; inferred as mild disagreement.

direct-action.rationale: Decentralized direct action and civil disobedience through affinity groups is the movement's main mode, from Bove's crop destruction to PGA action days.

means-match-ends.rationale: Horizontal organization and participatory methods are treated as prefiguring the world sought, particularly in anarchist-influenced networks.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Not advocated by any strand of the movement.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Only a radical fringe would say so; not a movement demand.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Socialist wing sympathetic, the reformist mainstream does not take a stance on communist distribution; split.

production-for-use.rationale: The critique of profit-driven commodification of water, seeds and education implies production for need, but it is not formulated this way.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Anti-capitalist wings say yes; many alter-globalists accept markets and target specific abuses, so adherents are split.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: The movement is anti-authoritarian, pluralist and non-partisan, and rejects party-led dictatorship.

collective-farming.rationale: Supports small farmers and peasant movements (MST, Thai peasants) rather than collectivization; inferred.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Anti-capitalists link capitalism and war and the movement opposed the Iraq war, but the reformist mainstream does not assert inevitability.

taxation-theft.rationale: A Tobin tax and redistribution are movement proposals; the movement rejects this libertarian view.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Collective and indigenous rights, workers' rights and the commons are central, so rights are not held to belong only to individuals.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Voice and democratic participation are central, and the movement wants more democratic say, not exit.

state-as-business.rationale: Rejects commodification and corporatization of public functions.

positive-liberty.rationale: Concern for livelihoods, labor and material conditions fits this view, though it is not framed in these terms.

media-academia-power.rationale: The movement stresses corporate media concentration and built independent media (Indymedia), rather than blaming universities and media over elected officials.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Opposes racism explicitly in PGA hallmarks and the movement's universalist outlook.

organic-representation.rationale: Not a movement idea; it favors participatory networks, though trade bodies and unions are coalition members.

total-state.rationale: The movement's grassroots, pluralist character clearly implies rejecting the total state, though only Wikipedia is cited.

national-rebirth.rationale: Nationalist radical-right strands that oppose globalization hold this, but the movement's mainstream disowns them.

territorial-expansion.rationale: The movement is anti-imperialist and anti-militarist.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Incompatible with its democratic and horizontal commitments.

bound-labor.rationale: Labor-rights emphasis and support for peasant land movements make bound labor anathema.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Critique of corporate-controlled science and patents shades toward it, but the movement takes no epistemological position.

universal-morality.rationale: Universal human rights language is used, but the movement is pluralist and not committed on moral epistemology.

single-common-good.rationale: Pluralist, 'movement of many movements' with no single doctrine, though the commons idea has a unifying pull.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: No documented movement position; the movement included both pro-Palestinian and other voices.

revive-national-language.rationale: Not addressed; cultural diversity concerns exist but nothing specific on state language revival.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Participatory ethos and worker control themes imply support, though not an explicit demand for votes on large-company governance.

school-vouchers.rationale: Klein cites students fighting commercialization of schools; the movement opposes privatizing education.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Opposes austerity and structural adjustment, so deficit-aversion is not endorsed.

economic-freedom.rationale: Rejects the idea that corporate economic freedom underpins liberty, charging that it erodes democracy.

rule-by-example.rationale: Not a movement idea; it emphasizes institutions and democratic participation.

national-self-determination.rationale: Left critics say trade rules erode national policy autonomy, but the movement is cosmopolitan and distrusts nationalism; self-determination in the democratic sense is endorsed.

force-without-un.rationale: The movement opposed the Iraq war and leaders' disregard for democracy over it (Chomsky).

reason-over-faith.rationale: Not addressed; religious activists such as Jubilee 2000 sit alongside secular ones.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: The left mainstream is universalist and No Border supporters reject the citizen-only premise.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Inferred from opposition to welfare cuts and conditionality as neoliberal policy.

class-collaboration.rationale: The movement sides with labor against corporations and does not frame employers as partners; reformist wings may differ.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Opposes the commodification of culture, and protects cultural diversity from homogenization; inferred.

dominated-front.rationale: Anti-imperialist sentiment exists, but the movement is not organized around state fronts of dominated countries.

workers-nation.rationale: The movement stresses cross-border unionization and international solidarity of workers.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Anti-patriarchy is named in PGA's revised hallmarks.

ban-interest.rationale: Jubilee debt-relief traditions touch on usury but a ban on interest is not a movement demand.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The movement's hallmarks oppose racism, which clearly implies rejecting segregation law; the support cited is Wikipedia only.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Anarchist and Marxist wings agree, while reformists see the state as capturable for democratic regulation; split.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Climate protection and environmentalism are central concerns.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: The left mainstream is pro-migrant and defends cultural diversity against homogenization.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy theory associated with the nationalist right, which the mainstream movement rejects.

proportional-representation.rationale: Inferred from democratic-participation commitments; not directly documented.

national-mission.rationale: Anti-imperialist; opposes exporting systems by force.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Opposition to patriarchy appears in the revised PGA hallmarks.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: The movement charges leaders and elites with contempt for democracy and capture by corporate power (Chomsky on the Iraq war).

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenics is incompatible with the movement's egalitarian human-rights outlook.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Genoa protest killing and police violence made accountability a live issue; inferred, not a formal demand.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The movement wants stronger public regulation and public services, the opposite of a minimal state.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: The movement's explicit anti-racism clearly implies rejecting this, though no source discusses it; the support is Wikipedia only.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Universalist, solidarity-based outlook and hallmarks opposing racism and patriarchy.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Not a concern of this movement.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Anti-colonialism is stated, but application to particular states is not a movement position.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Personal-law questions in particular states are not addressed by the movement, so no stance is documented.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from liberal-left and civil-liberty orientation.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: A religious-cultural issue of one region that the movement has never taken up.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Charge against global institutions is lack of democratic consent and accountability.

trade-surplus.rationale: A mercantilist export drive is not part of fair-trade thinking; the movement criticizes export-led dumping and rich-country dominance.

population-transfer.rationale: Its anti-racist, pro-migrant outlook clearly implies rejecting expulsions; the support is Wikipedia only.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Rejects competitive logic of corporate globalization in favor of solidarity and cooperation.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Not documented; the movement disowns far-right parties but anti-authoritarians are wary of party bans.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Resistance to unaccountable corporate and institutional power fits this idea, though the republican concept is not used.

vanguard-party.rationale: Movement is explicitly horizontal, decentralized and non-partisan.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Global justice and debt relief for poor countries are core aims.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Opposes privatization of public assets, but housing is peripheral; inferred.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Pro-labor; restrictions on labor action would be opposed.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: The movement attributes poverty to trade rules, debt and corporate power rather than population.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Left mainstream celebrates diversity and rejects this nationalist premise.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Participatory ideals could support sortition, but it is not a documented demand.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Defense of civil liberties against repression; inferred.

party-controls-media.rationale: The movement built independent outlets such as Indymedia against corporate and state control, which clearly implies rejection; the support is Wikipedia only.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Egalitarian ethos but no documented demand.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: The movement rejects party discipline and the WSF is non-partisan and non-representative.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Movement criticizes the EU's neoliberal design and loss of democratic control, though internationalist; majority wary.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church governance is outside the movement's concerns.

clerical-rule.rationale: Incompatible with secular-democratic values of the mainstream.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Movement opposed the Iraq war, but the revolutionary-defeatist stance is not stated.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Inferred from democratic and anti-concentration-of-power commitments.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: The movement is anti-authoritarian and does not defend strengthening socialist states; inferred from its anti-state-power and democratic stance.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Pacifist wings agree, while confrontational wings accept property damage and militant protest, so adherents split.

recall-officials.rationale: Participatory-democracy values imply support, though recall is not specifically demanded.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Anti-militarist sentiment and opposition to Iraq war suggest support, but it is not a stated program.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Peasant and farmer movements are valorized but the movement is largely urban and does not make this moral claim.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: The movement has no documented view on national reunification.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Movement is heavily student and academic-influenced; the claim is a populist-right theme.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Defends cultural diversity against homogenization, consistent with this view.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Secular-left mainstream and science-based environmental activism; inferred.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Not addressed; feminist and libertarian-left wings differ.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Ethnic-descent citizenship contradicts the pro-migrant mainstream.

minority-language-support.rationale: Defense of cultural diversity and indigenous rights suggests support.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Not addressed; religious-liberty claims are outside the movement's agenda.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Anarchist-influenced culture and 'tactical frivolity' suggest sympathy; inferred.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Debt cancellation for developing countries was demanded in Paris in 1989 and by Jubilee 2000, a standard demand of the movement.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: The movement holds that trade and finance regimes constrain poor countries' autonomy, so formal independence is not enough.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Democratic-participation values are sympathetic, but no movement text demands constituent assemblies.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Debt relief and global justice imply obligations of the rich, although the movement emphasizes fairer rules over charity.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Executive-selection rules are not a movement topic and no position is documented.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Critique of unaccountable institutions such as IMF suggests skepticism of insulated bodies.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from peace orientation.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: The commons framing treats shared and public interests as overriding enclosure and private appropriation.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Left and anarchist wings may say so; not a movement position.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Opposition to GM crops and corporate environmental risk reflects precaution.

collective-defense.rationale: Opposes military alliances in general; inferred.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Church-state institutional questions are not part of the movement's program.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The role of heads of state is not addressed by the movement.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Opposes military force and favors self-determination; inferred.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Autonomy arrangements between regions and states are not addressed, though local self-rule is valued.

sacred-ruler.rationale: A sacred head of state is never discussed; rejection is inferred from the movement's democratic and egalitarian outlook.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Redistributive orientation and Tobin-tax proposals oppose flat taxes.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Democratic accountability is a central demand, which clearly implies rejecting an unbound ruler; Wikipedia only.

space-expansion.rationale: Not a priority and associated with corporate techno-optimism; inferred.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Classical constitutional design is not addressed in the movement's texts.

leader-cult.rationale: Leader veneration is never discussed; rejection is inferred from the movement's leaderless, horizontal organisation.

equal-parenting.rationale: Family-court policy is not addressed by the movement.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Socialist-state internal politics is not a concern of this movement.

land-redistribution.rationale: Stiglitz, Korten and peasant movements like the MST that Klein cites argue for land reform and land occupations.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Nationalist claim rejected by the mainstream.

common-currency.rationale: Movement critics of the euro see loss of democratic control; not a stated plank.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Northern unions and NGOs pressed for binding labour and environmental clauses, but Southern groups such as Third World Network and the PGA's reject-the-WTO line opposed WTO social clauses as Northern protectionism, so the movement was split.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Inferred from the movement's stress on local self-determination and indigenous and minority rights against homogenizing global forces.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Inferred from the universalist, egalitarian framing that seeks equal rights and opposes racism in place rather than separate homelands.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Adherents are split: anti-capitalist currents stress economic structure while others stress democratic and moral claims; no shared line is documented.

ban-cartels.rationale: Inferred from the movement's attack on corporate concentration and power, though competition law is rarely its own demand.

no-bailouts.rationale: Inferred: the movement attacked IMF and corporate rescues that socialize losses, though it would favour public services over market discipline.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Inferred: the movement attacks WTO tribunals that override democratic decisions but values rights protections, so it does not back unchecked majorities.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: PGA hallmarks oppose patriarchy, so equal representation measures are inferred as supported.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Adherents are split: the localization strand favors local production while fair-trade internationalists reject walling off trade.

moral-incentives.rationale: The movement does not address what motivates work; no position is documented and none is strongly implied.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: The movement organizes through decentralized, largely nonviolent direct action and coalitions, and PGA hallmarks reject hierarchical vanguard methods.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Inferred from egalitarian, anti-colonial and anti-patriarchal hallmarks; no specific demand about titles is documented.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Inferred from the movement's internationalist, anti-ethnocentric outlook, which favours giving all regions' histories equal weight.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: The movement frames the IMF, World Bank and rich-country power as neocolonial and denies any right to rule others for their own good.

patriotic-education.rationale: Inferred: the left alter-globalization mainstream is internationalist and distrusts nationalism, which separates it from nationalist opponents of globalization.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Inferred: the movement's egalitarian outlook leans to support race-conscious remedies, though it does not campaign on the issue.

public-money-creation.rationale: Inferred: the movement wants democratic control of finance, but public money creation is a niche demand not found in its main programmes.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Inferred: participants see neoliberal capitalism as crisis-prone, but the movement mostly pursues reform and not collapse.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Inferred from its anti-imperialism: past rule gives no special claim to influence.

delink-world-market.rationale: Split: some strands favour delinking and relocalization, but the mainstream seeks fair rules and alternative integration.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: The movement stresses international solidarity of workers and labour in North and South, though it also highlights global inequality.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: The movement's egalitarian outlook and demands for strong regulation of corporations oppose a right to discriminate.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Inferred: it champions human rights but gives priority to participatory democracy over legal entrenchment, and adherents are split.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Anti-colonial and anti-imperialist solidarity is core; inferred that unfair imposed treaties are not binding.

elective-rulers.rationale: Democratic and anti-elite outlook opposes hereditary rule; inferred.

minority-veto.rationale: Consensus practice in direct-action networks suggests respect for dissent, but no stated principle.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Direct action and civil disobedience against illegitimate power are standard; inferred.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The movement demands democratic control over economic institutions; inferred support for elected legislatures over unaccountable power.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Many alter-globalization activists, especially environmentalists, extend concern to animals; inferred, not core.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Adherents are split between vegans and others.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: The movement frames global justice as rights and structural change, not charity from the privileged; inferred.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Inferred: the movement stresses ongoing racial and global North-South injustice, so it would not say racism has stopped being the main obstacle.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Inferred from its tradition of civil disobedience and direct action against laws it sees as serving corporations.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Inferred: the movement is split between technological optimists and those favouring degrowth and less work, and sources do not address automation.

multipolar-world.rationale: Inferred: it opposes domination by one economic power bloc and supports local and regional self-determination, though it also favours global solidarity.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Not addressed by the movement's sources, and its adherents range from Marxists to commons and ecological thinkers.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Inferred: the left mainstream is internationalist and distrusts nationalism, though it defends national and local sovereignty against corporate rules.

material-over-identity.rationale: Inferred: the movement is a coalition that includes feminist, indigenous and environmental causes alongside labour, so it would not subordinate them to workers' material interests.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Inferred: the movement is decentralised and anti-authoritarian, and its PGA-style hallmarks reject party-led rule.

missingStatements.text: Governments should tax international financial transactions, such as currency trades, to curb speculation and fund development.
missingStatements.rationale: The Tobin tax is part of the movement's standard agenda.
missingStatements.declined: A single policy instrument (the Tobin tax) rather than a position; its aim is covered by regulate-corporations and tax-the-wealthy.

missingStatements.text: International trade agreements should include binding labor and environmental standards.
missingStatements.rationale: Participants seek binding standards attached to any trade liberalization rather than none.

missingStatements.text: Public services such as water, education and health should be kept out of trade agreements and out of private hands.
missingStatements.rationale: Klein describes removing food safety, agriculture and water from trade deals and fighting privatization; 'the world is not for sale'.

missingStatements.text: Corporations should not have the legal rights of persons.
missingStatements.rationale: Ending corporate personhood is a stated aim of the movement.
missingStatements.declined: Narrow legal-doctrine claim (largely US constitutional law) that few other audited ideologies address; its aim is covered by regulate-corporations.

notes: The label covers both left internationalists and nationalist or Christian-right opponents of globalization; answers follow the left mainstream. Confidence is mostly low on social issues the movement never addressed. Some answers use sources read in summary only; PGA source s5 is cited for hallmarks but no answer relies solely on it.
